title: Power Apps: display density settings for model-driven apps
summary: The environment-default control gives the steps for adding a setting to a solution, but stops before the steps that actually change its environment value. The roadmap details, density behaviour and general SaveSettingValue API are supported.

claims.claim: Solutions > solution > Add existing > More > Setting is the UI path for changing the environment default display density.
claims.quote:
If the setting definition is available in the solution:
1. Select the setting definition.
2. In the Edit setting value dialog, in the Setting environment value section, select New value.
3. Provide the value, and then select Save.
claims.fix: The printed path only opens the add-existing-setting picker. Retain it in the note as the preliminary step for adding Display density to the solution. For the environment-value control, replace ui.path with 'Solutions > solution > Display density > Edit setting value > Setting environment value > New value'; the note should say to enter the desired value and select Save. This follows the cited guide's 'Adding a new setting environment value' procedure once the setting definition is in the solution.

claims.claim: POST <organization URI>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue with SettingName and Value sets a general organisation-level setting override.
claims.quote: Creates or updates app/organization level override. AppUniqueName: Model-driven app unique name (Optional). SettingName: Setting definition unique name (Required). Value: Overridden value that needs to be set (Required).

claims.claim: Makers open Settings on the app designer command bar to configure app settings.
claims.quote: In the app designer select Settings on the command bar.

claims.claim: POST <organization URI>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue with AppUniqueName, SettingName and Value sets a general app-level override.
claims.quote: Creates or updates app/organization level override. AppUniqueName: Model-driven app unique name (Optional). SettingName: Setting definition unique name (Required). Value: Overridden value that needs to be set (Required).

claims.claim: The settings guide's solution procedures require Solution preview on.
claims.quote: To follow the steps listed below you need to have Solution preview on.

claims.claim: The SaveSettingValue reference describes a general settings action rather than naming display density specifically.
claims.quote: Searched: "Display density" "SettingName" Power Apps. Opened the complete SaveSettingValue Action reference and appearance-settings page. The action reference names generic setting parameters, not density; the appearance page names no density-specific API.

claims.quote: Makers can suppress display density for an app by setting Display density to Off (enum value 0).

claims.claim: Save and publish the app for an app-settings change to apply.
claims.quote: You must select Publish to activate an app settings change. ... Save and Publish the app.

claims.claim: The three density levels are Comfortable, Cozy and Compact.
claims.quote: Comfortable: The default spacing that matches the modern, refreshed look. ... Cozy: A moderate reduction in vertical and horizontal spacing ... Compact: The tightest spacing

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft's density documentation describes no new business-data access, storage or sharing mechanism.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "display density" "data" "storage" "access". Opened appearance-settings and fluent-modern-theming; read UserSettings DisplayDensity. These describe presentation and saved preferences, not new business-data access, storage or sharing.

claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "display density" "permissions". Read appearance-settings and create-edit-configure-settings. The appearance page says admins and makers without naming security-role requirements.

claims.claim: The general settings guide describes an environment administrator adding an environment setting value.

claims.claim: The general settings guide describes an application author adding an app setting value.
claims.quote: an application author in the same environment above, can add a setting app value for the Async save handler setting for an app they are authoring

claims.claim: Only spacingVerticalS, spacingVerticalM, spacingVerticalL and spacingHorizontalL currently receive display-density adjustments.
claims.quote: spacingVerticalS ... spacingVerticalM ... spacingVerticalL ... spacingHorizontalL ... Only these spacing tokens currently receive display-density adjustments.

In the app designer, select Settings on the command bar.

claims.quote:
In a model-driven app, open the Settings menu on the app header.
Select Personal settings.
Select the Appearance tab.
Under Display density, select one of the following options:

claims.claim: The user's personal preference applies across their model-driven apps with wave 2 enabled.
claims.quote: This preference applies to every model-driven app that has the header and navigation refresh (wave 2) enabled.

claims.claim: Wave 2 availability may vary by region as build 2609.1 rolls out.
claims.quote: General availability begins with build 2609.1. Availability might vary by region as the build rolls out.

claims.claim: The general settings mechanism uses a definition's default value when no environment or app value overrides it.
claims.quote: It specifies the setting's value that will be used unless it is overridden by a setting environment value or a setting app value.

claims.claim: The general mechanism permits an app value to override both the definition's default and an environment value.
claims.quote: A setting app value can be used to override the default value, as specified in the setting definition, and the setting environment value (if one exists).

claims.claim: The pages read do not give the Display density setting definition's unique name for use with SaveSettingValue.
claims.quote: Searched: "Display density" "SettingName" Power Apps. Read appearance-settings, app-properties, create-edit-configure-settings and SaveSettingValue; none supplies the density setting definition's unique name.

claims.claim: Learn does not describe a control for enforcing a chosen density over a user's explicit personal choice.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "display density" "enforce". Read appearance-settings and create-edit-configure-settings: personal choices override defaults; Off suppresses density rather than enforcing a selected level.

claims.claim: Dataverse unbound Web API actions use POST to the organisation's versioned API path with parameters in a JSON body.
